parts:
Here is a clear, respectful, urgent email you can send to Ms. Mahand. It is calm but firm, asks for help without blaming, and keeps the focus on graduating on time.

:::writing{id="74831" variant="email" subject="Urgent Guidance Needed Regarding Dual Enrollment Math Credit"}
Dear Ms. Mahand,

I hope you are doing well. I am reaching out because I truly need your guidance and help as we are in a very time sensitive situation regarding my son, Donivan Hotchkiss, who is a senior.

Donivan failed his dual enrollment math class due to Columbia State not having a record of his final exam being submitted. We have gone back and forth extensively with the dual enrollment coordinator, the dean, and his instructor, but unfortunately no one has been able to resolve the issue or offer a solution. At this point, they have told us there is nothing further they can do.

This has put us in a very stressful position as graduation is approaching and we are now scrambling to find an alternative math option that would allow Donivan to stay on track and graduate on time.

I am hoping you might be able to advise us on any accelerated homeschool math courses that the school would approve, or if there is another institution besides Columbia State that you recommend where we could enroll him immediately to satisfy the requirement.

We are willing to move quickly and do whatever is necessary. I just need clarity on the best path forward and what the school will accept so we can act fast and avoid any delay in his graduation.

Thank you so much for your time, leadership, and support. I truly appreciate any direction you can provide us during this process.

Warm regards,  
Bethany Gifford  
Donivan Hotchkiss’s Mother  
:::
